## 6.3 Flange bolt torque

Table 6-2 gives the tightening torque for the CP-200 flange bolts. The values apply to bolts of property class 8.8, lightly oiled, with the spiral-wound gaskets supplied with the pump.

| Bolt size | Torque |
|---|---|
| M10 | 49 N·m |
| M12 | 85 N·m |
| M16 | 210 N·m |

Tighten the M12 flange bolts (property class 8.8, lightly oiled) to 85 N·m. Apply the torque in a cross pattern in three passes: 30 N·m, 60 N·m, then 85 N·m. Re-check the torque after the first 24 hours of operation.

Don't reuse spiral-wound gaskets. A gasket that has been compressed once won't seal at the specified torque.

evidence.title: CP-200 Troubleshooting Guide
evidence.section: CP-200 Troubleshooting Guide › 2 Controller error codes › Error E-217: seal-water pressure low

segments.text:
## Error E-217: seal-water pressure low

Error E-217 means seal-water pressure low. The controller trips the pump when seal-water pressure stays below 1.5 bar for 10 seconds, to protect the mechanical seal. Check that seal-water valve V-114 is open and that its strainer is clean, then reset the alarm at the local panel.

Common causes, most likely first:

1. Seal-water valve V-114 left closed or partly closed after maintenance.
2. A blocked strainer upstream of V-114 (work instruction WI-FS-031 describes the cleaning).
3. A failed pressure switch PS-31. Compare its reading with the local gauge.

To clear E-217, restore the seal-water pressure to at least 2.0 bar, wait until the alarm light stops flashing, then press RESET on the local panel. If the alarm returns within an hour, don't restart the pump again; raise a work order for the seal-water system.

segments.text:
# CP-200 Troubleshooting Guide

# 1 Using this guide

This guide explains the error codes that the CP-200 controller shows and the mechanical problems it can't detect. Each code's section says what the code means, when the controller raises it, the likely causes in the order to check them and how to clear it. Codes starting with E-1 concern the motor and its supply, E-2 the hydraulics and the seal, and E-3 the controller and its sensors.

Work through the causes in order. If you clear a code and it returns within an hour, stop and raise a work order instead of resetting it again.

## Error E-222: vibration high

Error E-222 means the vibration on the bearing housing exceeded 7.1 mm/s RMS. The controller warns at 4.5 mm/s RMS and trips the pump at 7.1 mm/s RMS.

Causes, most likely first:

1. Misalignment after maintenance.
2. Cavitation.
3. Worn bearings or a damaged impeller.

Section 3.1 describes how to find the cause. Don't restart the pump repeatedly after E-222.

evidence.section: CP-200 Troubleshooting Guide › 2 Controller error codes › Error E-106: supply undervoltage

segments.text:
## Error E-106: supply undervoltage

Error E-106 means the supply voltage stayed below 90 percent of its nominal value for more than 5 seconds. The pump restarts by itself 30 seconds after the voltage returns, unless automatic restart is disabled.

Causes, most likely first:

1. A weak supply during the start of another large motor.
2. A failing transformer tap changer.

E-106 clears itself. If it repeats, record the times and ask the plant electrical engineer to check the supply.

evidence.section: SOP-FS-014: Mechanical seal replacement on CP-200 pumps

segments.text:
# SOP-FS-014: Mechanical seal replacement on CP-200 pumps

Revision 3, effective September 14, 2026. This revision replaces PN-4471-B with PN-4471-C, following ECN-2291.

1. Apply lockout/tagout to the motor and isolate the seal-water and process lines, as safety bulletin SB-0932 requires. Verify zero energy.
2. Drain the casing and remove the coupling guard.
3. Remove the seal housing and the old seal. Inspect the shaft sleeve for scoring.
4. Fit mechanical seal PN-4471-C. Don't mix PN-4471-B and PN-4471-C parts.
5. Tighten the seal gland nuts evenly to 25 N·m.
6. Refit the coupling guard, remove the locks and tags, and start the pump as described in section 5.4 of the manual.
7. Record the seal's part number and the operating hours in the work order.

# HR guidance: parental leave changes for 2027

This guidance is restricted to HR and people managers until the change is announced on February 15, 2027. From March 1, 2027, paid parental leave increases from 16 to 20 weeks and can be taken in up to three blocks.

The six-month service requirement and full pay are unchanged. Employees whose leave starts before March 1, 2027 stay on the 2024 policy. Managers should send questions to their HR business partner.

## Questions managers may hear

Employees may ask whether they can split leave they have already started. They can't: the three-block rule applies only to leave that starts on or after March 1, 2027.

Employees on fixed-term contracts receive the same leave if their contract runs for at least six months beyond the start of the leave.

Employees with at least six months of service receive 16 weeks of paid parental leave after the birth or adoption of a child. The leave must be taken in one continuous block within 12 months of the birth or adoption, at 100 percent of base salary.

Employees agree the start date with their manager at least eight weeks in advance.

Issued after a near miss at the Riverside plant in 2026, when a seal housing was opened on a pump that was still under seal-water pressure.

Apply lockout/tagout (LOTO) to the motor and isolate the seal-water and process lines before opening any CP-200 seal housing. Verify zero energy before work starts.

Zero energy means that the motor can't start from the panel, the local pressure gauges read zero and the casing drain is open. Each person working on the pump fits their own lock.

This bulletin applies to every pump with a mechanical seal flushed by seal water, not only to the CP-200. Supervisors brief their teams on it before the next seal job and record the briefing.

At the Riverside plant, report any seal-water line that can't be isolated or drained to the Riverside maintenance planner on extension 4410 before work starts.

evidence.section: CP-200 Centrifugal Pump Operating and Maintenance Manual › 1 Safety

segments.text:
# 1 Safety

Read this manual before installing, operating or servicing the pump. Work on the pump only when you are trained for the task and the pump is isolated as your site's procedures require.

- Isolate the motor electrically and lock it out before any work on the pump.
- Release the pressure in the casing and the seal-water line before opening any connection.
- Wear safety glasses and gloves when handling the mechanical seal. The seal faces are brittle and their edges are sharp.
- Never run the pump dry or against a closed suction valve.
- Lift the pump only by the lifting lugs on the baseplate, never by the motor eyebolt.

segments.text:
# 4 Lubrication

## 4.1 Lubrication

The HG-400 is filled at the factory with 18 liters of ISO VG 220 mineral gear oil. Change the oil after the first 500 operating hours, then every 5,000 operating hours or every 12 months, whichever comes first. Synthetic PAO oil of the same viscosity extends the interval to 10,000 hours.

Check the oil level weekly at the sight glass with the gearbox stopped. In operation, the oil temperature must not exceed 90 °C.

## 4.2 Approved oils

Table 4-1 Approved oils

| Oil type | Viscosity grade | Change interval |
|---|---|---|
| Mineral gear oil | ISO VG 220 | 5,000 h or 12 months |
| Synthetic PAO gear oil | ISO VG 220 | 10,000 h or 24 months |
| Food-grade gear oil (NSF H1) | ISO VG 220 | 5,000 h or 12 months |

Don't mix mineral and synthetic oils. When changing from one type to the other, flush the gearbox with the new oil first.

evidence.section: SOP-MS-003: Oil change on HG-400 gearboxes

segments.text:
# SOP-MS-003: Oil change on HG-400 gearboxes

Revision 2, effective January 20, 2025. This procedure applies the oil change in section 4.3 of the HG-400 manual at Contoso plants and adds the checks that the plants' oil analysis program needs.

1. Lock out the driving motor as SOP-FS-007 describes for pumps; the same steps apply to gearboxes.
2. Take an oil sample from the middle of the sight glass level before draining, and label it with the gearbox tag.
3. Drain the warm oil, then clean and inspect the magnetic drain plug.
4. Refill with ISO VG 220 oil of the type on the gearbox's lubrication label: 18 liters for an HG-400.
5. Run the gearbox for ten minutes and check the level and the plugs for leaks.
6. Record the oil type, the quantity and the operating hours in the work order, and send the sample to the laboratory.

Gearbox GBX-07 on the Lakeside packaging line runs on synthetic PAO oil, so its change interval is 10,000 hours.

segments.text:
# RX flexible coupling: installation and alignment

Align the shafts with a dial indicator or a laser alignment tool after the gearbox and the motor are bolted down. Permissible misalignment for RX couplings up to size 90:

| Misalignment | Limit |
|---|---|
| Parallel offset | 0.05 mm |
| Angular | 0.05 mm per 100 mm |
| Axial gap | 3 mm ± 0.5 mm |

Re-check the alignment after the first 100 hours of operation, because the foundation settles. Replace the elastomer element when its teeth show cracks or are worn by more than 25 percent.

RX coupling sizes

| Size | Maximum bore | Maximum torque | Elastomer element |
|---|---|---|---|
| 50 | 50 mm | 450 N·m | PN-5120-A |
| 70 | 70 mm | 1,250 N·m | PN-5170-A |
| 90 | 90 mm | 2,800 N·m | PN-5190-A |
| 110 | 110 mm | 5,200 N·m | PN-5210-A |

For couplings above size 90, halve the permissible misalignment in the table above.

## 3.2 Mounting

Mount the HG-400 on a flat, rigid base; the mounting surface must be flat to within 0.1 mm. Use the four M16 foot bolts of property class 8.8 and tighten them to 195 N·m in a cross pattern.

Put shims under the feet, never under the gearbox housing. After mounting, align the input and output couplings as their installation instructions describe, and check that the breather plug on top of the housing is fitted and open.

evidence.section: CP-200 Troubleshooting Guide › 3 Mechanical problems › Troubleshooting: excessive vibration

segments.text:
# 3 Mechanical problems

## Troubleshooting: excessive vibration

Vibration above 4.5 mm/s RMS on the bearing housing needs investigation; above 7.1 mm/s RMS, stop the pump.

Likely causes, in the order to check them:

- Misalignment between the pump and motor shafts after maintenance. Check the coupling alignment.
- Cavitation, which sounds like gravel rattling in the casing. It comes from low suction pressure: check that the suction valve is fully open and the suction strainer is clean.
- Worn bearings. Bearing noise rises before the vibration does.
- A loose baseplate or loose foot bolts.
- A damaged or unbalanced impeller.

evidence.section: CP-200 Troubleshooting Guide › 2 Controller error codes › Error E-104: motor winding temperature high

segments.text:
## Error E-104: motor winding temperature high

Error E-104 means the motor's winding temperature exceeded 155 °C. The controller trips the pump and blocks a restart until the windings cool below 120 °C.

Check the motor's cooling fan and fan cover for blockages, and measure the supply voltage on all three phases; an unbalance of more than 2 percent overheats the windings. Frequent starts also cause E-104: the CP-200 motor allows no more than six starts per hour.

Reset E-104 at the local panel once the temperature has dropped. Never bypass the thermistor relay.

evidence.title: CP-200 Centrifugal Pump Operating and Maintenance Manual
evidence.section: CP-200 Centrifugal Pump Operating and Maintenance Manual › 2 Description

segments.text:
# 2 Description

The CP-200 is a single-stage, end-suction centrifugal pump with a closed impeller, designed for clean or slightly contaminated water at up to 90 °C. The pump and its motor sit on a common baseplate and are joined by a flexible spacer coupling, so the rotating assembly can be removed without disturbing the pipework.

The shaft is sealed by a cartridge mechanical seal flushed with clean seal water from an external supply. Two grease-lubricated ball bearings in the bearing housing carry the shaft. A controller on the pump skid monitors the motor, the bearing temperatures and the seal-water pressure and trips the pump when a limit is exceeded.

## Error E-231: liquid temperature high

Error E-231 means the liquid temperature in the casing exceeded 90 °C. The controller trips the pump after 10 seconds above the limit.

Causes, most likely first:

1. The pump ran against a closed discharge valve.
2. The process supplies liquid hotter than the pump's rating.

Let the casing cool and find out why the liquid overheated before resetting E-231.

evidence.title: VD-75 Variable Frequency Drive: Installation and Fault Guide
evidence.section: VD-75 Variable Frequency Drive: Installation and Fault Guide › 4 Faults

segments.text:
# 4 Faults

A fault stops the motor and shows its code on the display. Table 4-1 lists the faults; the most common ones have their own sections after the table. Reset a fault with the STOP/RESET key once its cause is removed.

Table 4-1 Fault codes

| Code | Fault | Likely cause | Remedy |
|---|---|---|---|
| F001 | DC bus undervoltage | Supply voltage dip or a missing phase | Check the supply; the drive restarts when the voltage returns |
| F002 | DC bus overvoltage | Ramp-down time too short for the load's inertia | Raise parameter 2-11 or fit a brake resistor |
| F003 | Heatsink overtemperature | Blocked air flow or a failed fan | Clean the air path; check the fan (F016) |
| F004 | Earth fault | Damaged motor cable or wet motor | Measure the insulation before resetting |
| F005 | Motor overload (I²t) | Motor current above its rating for too long | Check the load; check parameter 1-03 |
| F006 | Input phase loss | A blown supply fuse | Replace the fuse and find out why it blew |
| F007 | Motor phase loss | Loose motor cable terminal | Tighten the motor terminals |
| F008 | Fieldbus timeout | No message from the controller for 2 seconds | Check the network cable and the controller |
| F009 | Brake resistor overload | Too many fast stops | Lengthen the ramp-down time |
| F010 | Analog input lost | Speed reference below 2 mA on a 4 to 20 mA input | Check the reference cable and its source |
| F011 | Output short circuit | Short circuit in the motor cable or motor | Disconnect and test the motor cable |
| F013 | Motor stall | Motor below 5 percent of set speed at full current | Free the jammed load |
| F015 | Parameter memory error | Corrupt parameters after a power cut during a save | Restore the parameter backup |
| F016 | Cooling fan failure | Fan blocked or worn out | Replace fan PN-7716-A |
| F017 | External fault | The external fault input opened | Check the device wired to the input |
| F018 | Safe torque off active | The safety circuit removed the enable signal | Close the safety circuit, then reset |
| F020 | Overspeed | Motor speed above 120 percent of maximum frequency | Check the load for overhauling forces |
| F021 | Underload | Motor current below 15 percent while running | Check for a broken belt or coupling |

## Fault F012: output overcurrent

Fault F012 means the drive's output current exceeded 200 percent of its rating. The drive stops the motor at once to protect its output stage.

Check for a jammed load, such as a blocked conveyor or a seized gearbox, and for a short circuit in the motor cable. A ramp-up time that is too short also causes F012: raise parameter 2-10 (ramp-up time) from 2 to 5 seconds. Reset F012 with the STOP/RESET key once the cause is removed.

## Fault F002: DC bus overvoltage

Fault F002 means the voltage of the drive's internal DC bus exceeded 800 V. It happens when the motor feeds energy back into the drive faster than the drive can absorb it, usually during a fast stop of a heavy load. Raise parameter 2-11 (ramp-down time), or fit a brake resistor if the process needs fast stops.

## Fault F010: analog input lost

Fault F010 means the speed reference on a 4 to 20 mA input fell below 2 mA, which the drive reads as a broken wire. The drive stops the motor rather than run at an unknown speed. Check the reference cable and the device that sends the signal.

| F008 | Fieldbus timeout | No message from the controller for 2 seconds | Check the network cable and the controller |
| F009 | Brake resistor overload | Too many fast stops | Lengthen the ramp-down time |
| F010 | Analog input lost | Speed reference below 2 mA on a 4 to 20 mA input | Check the reference cable and its source |
| F011 | Output short circuit | Short circuit in the motor cable or motor | Disconnect and test the motor cable |
| F013 | Motor stall | Motor below 5 percent of set speed at full current | Free the jammed load |
| F015 | Parameter memory error | Corrupt parameters after a power cut during a save | Restore the parameter backup |
| F016 | Cooling fan failure | Fan blocked or worn out | Replace fan PN-7716-A |
| F017 | External fault | The external fault input opened | Check the device wired to the input |
| F018 | Safe torque off active | The safety circuit removed the enable signal | Close the safety circuit, then reset |
| F020 | Overspeed | Motor speed above 120 percent of maximum frequency | Check the load for overhauling forces |
| F021 | Underload | Motor current below 15 percent while running | Check for a broken belt or coupling |
## Fault F012: output overcurrent

Fault F012 means the drive's output current exceeded 200 percent of its rating. The drive stops the motor at once to protect its output stage.

Check for a jammed load, such as a blocked conveyor or a seized gearbox, and for a short circuit in the motor cable. A ramp-up time that is too short also causes F012: raise parameter 2-10 (ramp-up time) from 2 to 5 seconds. Reset F012 with the STOP/RESET key once the cause is removed.
## Fault F002: DC bus overvoltage

Fault F002 means the voltage of the drive's internal DC bus exceeded 800 V. It happens when the motor feeds energy back into the drive faster than the drive can absorb it, usually during a fast stop of a heavy load. Raise parameter 2-11 (ramp-down time), or fit a brake resistor if the process needs fast stops.
## Fault F010: analog input lost

Fault F010 means the speed reference on a 4 to 20 mA input fell below 2 mA, which the drive reads as a broken wire. The drive stops the motor rather than run at an unknown speed. Check the reference cable and the device that sends the signal.

# Procurement policy PROC-POL-007: Purchase approvals

Every purchase order needs an approver other than the requester. Orders above 25,000 USD need a second approval from the plant controller, and orders above 250,000 USD need the CFO's approval.

Buy only from qualified suppliers. A new supplier is qualified after a quality audit and a credit check, and Procurement re-qualifies each supplier every three years.

Approval limits

| Order value | Approvals needed |
|---|---|
| Up to 25,000 USD | One approver other than the requester |
| 25,000 to 250,000 USD | The approver and the plant controller |
| Above 250,000 USD | The approver, the plant controller and the CFO |

Splitting an order to stay under an approval limit is a breach of this policy. Emergency orders outside working hours may be placed by the duty manager and approved on the next business day.

Welding, grinding and cutting outside the workshops need a hot work permit from the shift supervisor. Remove or cover combustible material within 10 meters, keep a fire extinguisher at the work site and post a fire watch for 60 minutes after the work ends.

segments.text:
# CP-200 Centrifugal Pump Operating and Maintenance Manual

Edition 2009. Contoso Industrial, Fluid Systems division. Keep this manual with the pump for the life of the equipment and pass it on with the pump if it is moved or sold.

# 1 Safety

Read this manual before installing, operating or servicing the pump. Work on the pump only when you are trained for the task and the pump is isolated as your site's procedures require.

- Isolate the motor electrically and lock it out before any work on the pump.
- Release the pressure in the casing and the seal-water line before opening any connection.
- Wear safety glasses and gloves when handling the mechanical seal. The seal faces are brittle and their edges are sharp.
- Never run the pump dry or against a closed suction valve.
- Lift the pump only by the lifting lugs on the baseplate, never by the motor eyebolt.

evidence.section: CP-200 Troubleshooting Guide › 1 Using this guide

segments.text:
# CP-200 Troubleshooting Guide

# 1 Using this guide

This guide explains the error codes that the CP-200 controller shows and the mechanical problems it can't detect. Each code's section says what the code means, when the controller raises it, the likely causes in the order to check them and how to clear it. Codes starting with E-1 concern the motor and its supply, E-2 the hydraulics and the seal, and E-3 the controller and its sensors.

Work through the causes in order. If you clear a code and it returns within an hour, stop and raise a work order instead of resetting it again.

segments.text:
# Field service report SR-2026-1213

Customer: Woodgrove Foods, packaging line 2. Engineer: Kwame Asante. Date: December 13, 2026.

Complaint: a whining noise from the HG-400 gearbox that rose with speed.

Findings: the oil level was below the sight glass and the oil had darkened; the last oil change was 14 months earlier. The first-stage gear teeth showed light pitting.

Work done: drained and flushed the gearbox, refilled it with 18 liters of ISO VG 220 oil and replaced a leaking output shaft seal. The noise dropped to normal. Recommended an oil analysis every six months.

evidence.title: CP-200 Centrifugal Pump Operating and Maintenance Manual
evidence.section: CP-200 Centrifugal Pump Operating and Maintenance Manual › 6 Assembly and disassembly › 6.3 Flange bolt torque

segments.text:
## 6.3 Flange bolt torque

Table 6-2 gives the tightening torque for the CP-200 flange bolts. The values apply to bolts of property class 8.8, lightly oiled, with the spiral-wound gaskets supplied with the pump.

| Bolt size | Torque |
|---|---|
| M10 | 49 N·m |
| M12 | 85 N·m |
| M16 | 210 N·m |

Tighten the M12 flange bolts (property class 8.8, lightly oiled) to 85 N·m. Apply the torque in a cross pattern in three passes: 30 N·m, 60 N·m, then 85 N·m. Re-check the torque after the first 24 hours of operation.

Don't reuse spiral-wound gaskets. A gasket that has been compressed once won't seal at the specified torque.

## 6.4 Seal housing bolts

Tighten the four seal housing bolts to 45 N·m. Fit the seal housing before the bearing housing is bolted back to the casing, so that the seal can be centered on the shaft.

evidence.title: SOP-FS-014: Mechanical seal replacement on CP-200 pumps
evidence.section: SOP-FS-014: Mechanical seal replacement on CP-200 pumps

segments.text:
# SOP-FS-014: Mechanical seal replacement on CP-200 pumps

Revision 3, effective September 14, 2026. This revision replaces PN-4471-B with PN-4471-C, following ECN-2291.

1. Apply lockout/tagout to the motor and isolate the seal-water and process lines, as safety bulletin SB-0932 requires. Verify zero energy.
2. Drain the casing and remove the coupling guard.
3. Remove the seal housing and the old seal. Inspect the shaft sleeve for scoring.
4. Fit mechanical seal PN-4471-C. Don't mix PN-4471-B and PN-4471-C parts.
5. Tighten the seal gland nuts evenly to 25 N·m.
6. Refit the coupling guard, remove the locks and tags, and start the pump as described in section 5.4 of the manual.
7. Record the seal's part number and the operating hours in the work order.

evidence.section: CP-200 Centrifugal Pump Operating and Maintenance Manual › 7 Maintenance › 7.2 Service intervals

segments.text:
## 7.2 Service intervals

Inspect the mechanical seal and the bearings every 2,000 operating hours or six months, whichever comes first. Replace mechanical seal PN-4471-B every 8,000 operating hours.

| Task | Interval |
|---|---|
| Inspect the mechanical seal and the bearings | 2,000 h or 6 months |
| Regrease the bearings (lithium-complex grease, 15 g per bearing) | 4,000 h |
| Check the coupling alignment | 12 months |
| Replace mechanical seal PN-4471-B | 8,000 h |
| Replace the bearings | 32,000 h |

Record every inspection in the maintenance log with the operating hours from the hour meter. Halve the intervals for pumps that handle abrasive liquids or run above 60 °C.

## Bearing overheating

Bearings run hottest in the first hours after regreasing, while excess grease is pushed out. A bearing that stays above 85 °C has too much grease, too little grease, a misaligned coupling or wear. Check the alignment and the amount of grease before replacing the bearing.

evidence.title: CP-200 Troubleshooting Guide
evidence.section: CP-200 Troubleshooting Guide › 2 Controller error codes › Error E-221: bearing temperature high

segments.text:
## Error E-221: bearing temperature high

Error E-221 means a bearing temperature exceeded 95 °C. The controller warns at 85 °C and trips the pump at 95 °C.

Causes, most likely first:

1. Too much grease after regreasing.
2. Misalignment between pump and motor.
3. A worn bearing.

Let the bearings cool, check the alignment and the amount of grease, then reset E-221.

evidence.section: CP-200 Centrifugal Pump Operating and Maintenance Manual › 9 Troubleshooting

segments.text:
# 9 Troubleshooting

The controller shows an error code for most faults; the CP-200 troubleshooting guide explains each code. Table 9-1 lists faults that the controller can't detect.

Table 9-1 Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Possible cause | Remedy |
|---|---|---|
| Pump doesn't deliver | Suction valve closed or casing not vented | Open the suction valve fully and vent the casing |
| Delivery falls off over weeks | Worn wear ring or impeller | Check the impeller clearance (section 6.2) |
| High bearing temperature | Too much or too little grease | Regrease as section 7.3 describes |
| Seal leaks steadily | Worn seal faces | Replace the mechanical seal (section 8.1) |
| Motor overloads | Pump runs far right of its curve | Throttle the discharge valve to the duty point |

evidence.title: CP-200 Centrifugal Pump Operating and Maintenance Manual
evidence.section: CP-200 Centrifugal Pump Operating and Maintenance Manual › 2 Description

segments.text:
# 2 Description

The CP-200 is a single-stage, end-suction centrifugal pump with a closed impeller, designed for clean or slightly contaminated water at up to 90 °C. The pump and its motor sit on a common baseplate and are joined by a flexible spacer coupling, so the rotating assembly can be removed without disturbing the pipework.

The shaft is sealed by a cartridge mechanical seal flushed with clean seal water from an external supply. Two grease-lubricated ball bearings in the bearing housing carry the shaft. A controller on the pump skid monitors the motor, the bearing temperatures and the seal-water pressure and trips the pump when a limit is exceeded.

evidence.title: Engineering change notice ECN-2291: CP-200 mechanical seal
evidence.section: Engineering change notice ECN-2291: CP-200 mechanical seal › Engineering change notice ECN-2291

segments.text:
# Engineering change notice ECN-2291

| Field | Entry |
|---|---|
| Change notice | ECN-2291 |
| Title | CP-200 mechanical seal |
| Product | CP-200 centrifugal pump, all sizes |
| Originator | Nadia Rahman, reliability engineering |
| Date raised | August 21, 2026 |
| Effective | September 14, 2026 |

Effective September 14, 2026, mechanical seal PN-4471-B is superseded by PN-4471-C on all CP-200 pumps. PN-4471-C has a silicon-carbide face rated for higher seal-water temperatures. Fit PN-4471-C at the next seal replacement and quarantine remaining PN-4471-B stock.

Reason for the change: three PN-4471-B failures in 2026 were traced to wear of the carbon face at seal-water temperatures above 60 °C.

Affected documents: CP-200 manual (2009) sections 7.2 and 8.1, and SOP-FS-014. The manual will be revised in 2027; until then, this notice takes precedence over it.

Approved by Nadia Rahman, reliability engineering.

Affected parts

| Old part | New part | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| PN-4471-B | PN-4471-C | Quarantine remaining stock; return to Fabrikam Seals for credit |

Distribution: Fluid Systems maintenance planners at all four plants, Field Services, Procurement and the stores.

evidence.section: Engineering change notice ECN-2240: CP-200 casing wear ring material › Engineering change notice ECN-2240

segments.text:
# Engineering change notice ECN-2240

| Field | Entry |
|---|---|
| Change notice | ECN-2240 |
| Title | CP-200 casing wear ring material |
| Product | CP-200 centrifugal pump, all sizes |
| Originator | Nadia Rahman, reliability engineering |
| Date raised | January 27, 2025 |
| Effective | March 1, 2025 |

Effective March 1, 2025, casing wear ring PN-2840-A (bronze) is superseded by PN-2840-B (carbon-filled PTFE composite) on all CP-200 pumps. The composite ring tolerates brief dry running without seizing, and its smaller running clearance of 0.25 mm improves efficiency by about 2 percent.

Fit PN-2840-B whenever a wear ring is replaced. The bronze rings in stock may be used up on pumps that handle liquids above 80 °C, where the composite ring is not approved.

Affected parts

| Old part | New part | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| PN-2840-A | PN-2840-B | Use up stock on pumps above 80 °C only |

Affected documents: CP-200 manual (2009) sections 6.2 and 8.1.

evidence.section: CP-200 Troubleshooting Guide › 2 Controller error codes › Error E-102: supply phase missing

segments.text:
## Error E-102: supply phase missing

Error E-102 means one of the three supply phases is missing. The controller checks the phases at every start and once a second while the pump runs.

Causes, most likely first:

1. A blown fuse in the motor feeder.
2. A loose terminal in the motor control center.

Have an electrician check the fuses and terminals. E-102 clears itself when all three phases return.

## Error E-103: wrong phase sequence

Error E-103 means the supply phase sequence is reversed, so the pump would run backwards. The controller blocks the start; it never trips a running pump for E-103.

Causes, most likely first:

1. Two supply cables were swapped during electrical work.

Have an electrician swap two phases at the motor terminal box, then confirm the direction of rotation against the arrow on the bearing housing.

## Error E-104: motor winding temperature high

Error E-104 means the motor's winding temperature exceeded 155 °C. The controller trips the pump and blocks a restart until the windings cool below 120 °C.

Check the motor's cooling fan and fan cover for blockages, and measure the supply voltage on all three phases; an unbalance of more than 2 percent overheats the windings. Frequent starts also cause E-104: the CP-200 motor allows no more than six starts per hour.

Reset E-104 at the local panel once the temperature has dropped. Never bypass the thermistor relay.

evidence.title: CP-200 Centrifugal Pump Operating and Maintenance Manual
evidence.section: CP-200 Centrifugal Pump Operating and Maintenance Manual › 5 Commissioning › 5.1 Checks before the first start

segments.text:
# 5 Commissioning

## 5.1 Checks before the first start

1. Check that the rotating assembly turns freely by hand.
2. Check the coupling alignment and fit the coupling guard.
3. Check that the bearings are greased; pumps leave the factory greased for 4,000 hours.
4. Flush the suction pipe and the seal-water line before connecting them.

## 5.4 Start-up

Before the first start, and after any work on the seal or the impeller, prime the pump and check the seal-water supply.

1. Open the suction valve fully. Never throttle the suction side.
2. Vent the casing at the vent plug until water flows without air.
3. Open the seal-water supply and confirm a pressure of 2.0 to 3.0 bar at the seal flush connection. The seal-water pressure must exceed the suction pressure by at least 1 bar.
4. Open the discharge valve about one quarter.
5. Jog the motor and confirm the direction of rotation against the arrow on the bearing housing.
6. Start the pump, then open the discharge valve slowly to the duty point within two minutes. Running against a closed discharge valve for longer overheats the liquid in the casing.

During the first hour, check that the bearing temperatures stay below 80 °C and listen for cavitation noise.

evidence.title: Safety bulletin SB-0932: Seal housing work (Northgate plant)
evidence.section: Safety bulletin SB-0932: Seal housing work (Northgate plant) › Safety bulletin SB-0932: Seal housing work

segments.text:
# Safety bulletin SB-0932: Seal housing work

Issued after a near miss at the Riverside plant in 2026, when a seal housing was opened on a pump that was still under seal-water pressure.

Apply lockout/tagout (LOTO) to the motor and isolate the seal-water and process lines before opening any CP-200 seal housing. Verify zero energy before work starts.

Zero energy means that the motor can't start from the panel, the local pressure gauges read zero and the casing drain is open. Each person working on the pump fits their own lock.

This bulletin applies to every pump with a mechanical seal flushed by seal water, not only to the CP-200. Supervisors brief their teams on it before the next seal job and record the briefing.

At the Northgate plant, report any seal-water line that can't be isolated or drained to the Northgate maintenance planner on extension 5417 before work starts.

evidence.title: CP-200 Troubleshooting Guide
evidence.section: CP-200 Troubleshooting Guide › 3 Mechanical problems › Seal leakage

segments.text:
## Seal leakage

A new mechanical seal may drip for the first few hours while its faces run in. A seal that leaks steadily after that has worn or damaged faces. The most common causes are dry running, seal-water pressure below 1.5 bar and abrasive particles in the seal water. Replace the seal as SOP-FS-014 describes; don't try to stop a leak by tightening the gland nuts beyond their torque.

evidence.title: SOP-FS-014: Mechanical seal replacement on CP-200 pumps
evidence.section: SOP-FS-014: Mechanical seal replacement on CP-200 pumps

segments.text:
# SOP-FS-014: Mechanical seal replacement on CP-200 pumps

Revision 3, effective September 14, 2026. This revision replaces PN-4471-B with PN-4471-C, following ECN-2291.

1. Apply lockout/tagout to the motor and isolate the seal-water and process lines, as safety bulletin SB-0932 requires. Verify zero energy.
2. Drain the casing and remove the coupling guard.
3. Remove the seal housing and the old seal. Inspect the shaft sleeve for scoring.
4. Fit mechanical seal PN-4471-C. Don't mix PN-4471-B and PN-4471-C parts.
5. Tighten the seal gland nuts evenly to 25 N·m.
6. Refit the coupling guard, remove the locks and tags, and start the pump as described in section 5.4 of the manual.
7. Record the seal's part number and the operating hours in the work order.

evidence.title: VD-75 Variable Frequency Drive: Installation and Fault Guide
evidence.section: VD-75 Variable Frequency Drive: Installation and Fault Guide › 4 Faults

segments.text:
# 4 Faults

A fault stops the motor and shows its code on the display. Table 4-1 lists the faults; the most common ones have their own sections after the table. Reset a fault with the STOP/RESET key once its cause is removed.

Table 4-1 Fault codes

| Code | Fault | Likely cause | Remedy |
|---|---|---|---|
| F001 | DC bus undervoltage | Supply voltage dip or a missing phase | Check the supply; the drive restarts when the voltage returns |
| F002 | DC bus overvoltage | Ramp-down time too short for the load's inertia | Raise parameter 2-11 or fit a brake resistor |
| F003 | Heatsink overtemperature | Blocked air flow or a failed fan | Clean the air path; check the fan (F016) |
| F004 | Earth fault | Damaged motor cable or wet motor | Measure the insulation before resetting |
| F005 | Motor overload (I²t) | Motor current above its rating for too long | Check the load; check parameter 1-03 |
| F006 | Input phase loss | A blown supply fuse | Replace the fuse and find out why it blew |
| F007 | Motor phase loss | Loose motor cable terminal | Tighten the motor terminals |
| F008 | Fieldbus timeout | No message from the controller for 2 seconds | Check the network cable and the controller |
| F009 | Brake resistor overload | Too many fast stops | Lengthen the ramp-down time |
| F010 | Analog input lost | Speed reference below 2 mA on a 4 to 20 mA input | Check the reference cable and its source |
| F011 | Output short circuit | Short circuit in the motor cable or motor | Disconnect and test the motor cable |
| F013 | Motor stall | Motor below 5 percent of set speed at full current | Free the jammed load |
| F015 | Parameter memory error | Corrupt parameters after a power cut during a save | Restore the parameter backup |
| F016 | Cooling fan failure | Fan blocked or worn out | Replace fan PN-7716-A |
| F017 | External fault | The external fault input opened | Check the device wired to the input |
| F018 | Safe torque off active | The safety circuit removed the enable signal | Close the safety circuit, then reset |
| F020 | Overspeed | Motor speed above 120 percent of maximum frequency | Check the load for overhauling forces |
| F021 | Underload | Motor current below 15 percent while running | Check for a broken belt or coupling |

## Fault F012: output overcurrent

Fault F012 means the drive's output current exceeded 200 percent of its rating. The drive stops the motor at once to protect its output stage.

Check for a jammed load, such as a blocked conveyor or a seized gearbox, and for a short circuit in the motor cable. A ramp-up time that is too short also causes F012: raise parameter 2-10 (ramp-up time) from 2 to 5 seconds. Reset F012 with the STOP/RESET key once the cause is removed.

## Fault F002: DC bus overvoltage

Fault F002 means the voltage of the drive's internal DC bus exceeded 800 V. It happens when the motor feeds energy back into the drive faster than the drive can absorb it, usually during a fast stop of a heavy load. Raise parameter 2-11 (ramp-down time), or fit a brake resistor if the process needs fast stops.

## Fault F010: analog input lost

Fault F010 means the speed reference on a 4 to 20 mA input fell below 2 mA, which the drive reads as a broken wire. The drive stops the motor rather than run at an unknown speed. Check the reference cable and the device that sends the signal.

# 4 Lubrication

## 4.1 Lubrication

The HG-400 is filled at the factory with 18 liters of ISO VG 220 mineral gear oil. Change the oil after the first 500 operating hours, then every 5,000 operating hours or every 12 months, whichever comes first. Synthetic PAO oil of the same viscosity extends the interval to 10,000 hours.

Check the oil level weekly at the sight glass with the gearbox stopped. In operation, the oil temperature must not exceed 90 °C.

## 4.2 Approved oils

Table 4-1 Approved oils

| Oil type | Viscosity grade | Change interval |
|---|---|---|
| Mineral gear oil | ISO VG 220 | 5,000 h or 12 months |
| Synthetic PAO gear oil | ISO VG 220 | 10,000 h or 24 months |
| Food-grade gear oil (NSF H1) | ISO VG 220 | 5,000 h or 12 months |

Don't mix mineral and synthetic oils. When changing from one type to the other, flush the gearbox with the new oil first.

## Error E-201: suction pressure low

evidence.section: CP-200 Troubleshooting Guide › 2 Controller error codes › Error E-101: motor overload

segments.text:
## Error E-101: motor overload

Error E-101 means the motor current stayed above the overload setting for longer than the trip delay. The overload relay trips after 10 seconds above 110 percent of the motor's rated current.

Causes, most likely first:

1. The pump runs far to the right of its curve because the discharge valve is open too far.
2. The impeller rubs on the wear ring after a bearing failure.
3. The overload relay is set below the motor's rated current.

Find and remove the cause, then reset E-101 at the local panel. The relay resets itself after two minutes.

evidence.title: CP-200 Troubleshooting Guide
evidence.section: CP-200 Troubleshooting Guide › 2 Controller error codes › Error E-217: seal-water pressure low

segments.text:
## Error E-217: seal-water pressure low

Error E-217 means seal-water pressure low. The controller trips the pump when seal-water pressure stays below 1.5 bar for 10 seconds, to protect the mechanical seal. Check that seal-water valve V-114 is open and that its strainer is clean, then reset the alarm at the local panel.

Common causes, most likely first:

1. Seal-water valve V-114 left closed or partly closed after maintenance.
2. A blocked strainer upstream of V-114 (work instruction WI-FS-031 describes the cleaning).
3. A failed pressure switch PS-31. Compare its reading with the local gauge.

To clear E-217, restore the seal-water pressure to at least 2.0 bar, wait until the alarm light stops flashing, then press RESET on the local panel. If the alarm returns within an hour, don't restart the pump again; raise a work order for the seal-water system.

evidence.title: WI-FS-031: Cleaning the seal-water strainer upstream of V-114
evidence.section: WI-FS-031: Cleaning the seal-water strainer upstream of V-114

segments.text:
# WI-FS-031: Cleaning the seal-water strainer upstream of V-114

The seal-water line to pump P-201 has a Y-strainer with a 100-micron screen upstream of valve V-114. A blocked screen is the most common cause of error E-217 at the Riverside plant.

1. Stop P-201 and close the isolation valve upstream of the strainer. Leave V-114 open.
2. Put a bucket under the strainer and release the pressure through the blow-down valve.
3. Unscrew the strainer cap, pull out the screen and rinse it with clean water. Replace the screen if it is torn.
4. Refit the screen with a new cap gasket and open the isolation valve.
5. Check that the gauge shows a seal-water pressure of 2.0 to 3.0 bar.

Clean the screen every three months, and whenever E-217 trips.

evidence.section: VD-75 Variable Frequency Drive: Installation and Fault Guide › 4 Faults

segments.text:
# 4 Faults

A fault stops the motor and shows its code on the display. Table 4-1 lists the faults; the most common ones have their own sections after the table. Reset a fault with the STOP/RESET key once its cause is removed.

Table 4-1 Fault codes

| Code | Fault | Likely cause | Remedy |
|---|---|---|---|
| F001 | DC bus undervoltage | Supply voltage dip or a missing phase | Check the supply; the drive restarts when the voltage returns |
| F002 | DC bus overvoltage | Ramp-down time too short for the load's inertia | Raise parameter 2-11 or fit a brake resistor |
| F003 | Heatsink overtemperature | Blocked air flow or a failed fan | Clean the air path; check the fan (F016) |

evidence.title: WI-FS-031: Cleaning the seal-water strainer upstream of V-114
evidence.section: WI-FS-031: Cleaning the seal-water strainer upstream of V-114

segments.text:
# WI-FS-031: Cleaning the seal-water strainer upstream of V-114

The seal-water line to pump P-201 has a Y-strainer with a 100-micron screen upstream of valve V-114. A blocked screen is the most common cause of error E-217 at the Riverside plant.

1. Stop P-201 and close the isolation valve upstream of the strainer. Leave V-114 open.
2. Put a bucket under the strainer and release the pressure through the blow-down valve.
3. Unscrew the strainer cap, pull out the screen and rinse it with clean water. Replace the screen if it is torn.
4. Refit the screen with a new cap gasket and open the isolation valve.
5. Check that the gauge shows a seal-water pressure of 2.0 to 3.0 bar.

Clean the screen every three months, and whenever E-217 trips.

evidence.title: CP-200 Troubleshooting Guide
evidence.section: CP-200 Troubleshooting Guide › 2 Controller error codes › Error E-217: seal-water pressure low

segments.text:
## Error E-217: seal-water pressure low

Error E-217 means seal-water pressure low. The controller trips the pump when seal-water pressure stays below 1.5 bar for 10 seconds, to protect the mechanical seal. Check that seal-water valve V-114 is open and that its strainer is clean, then reset the alarm at the local panel.

Common causes, most likely first:

1. Seal-water valve V-114 left closed or partly closed after maintenance.
2. A blocked strainer upstream of V-114 (work instruction WI-FS-031 describes the cleaning).
3. A failed pressure switch PS-31. Compare its reading with the local gauge.

To clear E-217, restore the seal-water pressure to at least 2.0 bar, wait until the alarm light stops flashing, then press RESET on the local panel. If the alarm returns within an hour, don't restart the pump again; raise a work order for the seal-water system.

evidence.section: CP-200 Troubleshooting Guide › 2 Controller error codes › Error E-201: suction pressure low

segments.text:
## Error E-201: suction pressure low

Error E-201 means the suction pressure fell below 0.3 bar. The controller warns for 20 seconds before it trips the pump, to ride through short dips.

Causes, most likely first:

1. The suction valve is partly closed.
2. The suction strainer is blocked.
3. The level in the suction tank is too low.

Open the suction valve fully, clean the suction strainer and check the tank level before resetting E-201.

## Error E-302: seal-water pressure switch fault

Error E-302 means pressure switch PS-31 reports pressure while the seal-water supply is closed. The controller checks PS-31 each time the seal-water valve closes.

Causes, most likely first:

1. A stuck pressure switch.
2. A short circuit in the switch cable.

Replace PS-31. Until it is replaced, check the seal-water pressure at the local gauge every shift.

evidence.section: CP-200 Troubleshooting Guide › 3 Mechanical problems › Seal leakage

segments.text:
## Seal leakage

A new mechanical seal may drip for the first few hours while its faces run in. A seal that leaks steadily after that has worn or damaged faces. The most common causes are dry running, seal-water pressure below 1.5 bar and abrasive particles in the seal water. Replace the seal as SOP-FS-014 describes; don't try to stop a leak by tightening the gland nuts beyond their torque.

evidence.section: HR guidance: parental leave changes for 2027

segments.text:
# HR guidance: parental leave changes for 2027

This guidance is restricted to HR and people managers until the change is announced on February 15, 2027. From March 1, 2027, paid parental leave increases from 16 to 20 weeks and can be taken in up to three blocks.

The six-month service requirement and full pay are unchanged. Employees whose leave starts before March 1, 2027 stay on the 2024 policy. Managers should send questions to their HR business partner.

## Questions managers may hear

Employees may ask whether they can split leave they have already started. They can't: the three-block rule applies only to leave that starts on or after March 1, 2027.

Employees on fixed-term contracts receive the same leave if their contract runs for at least six months beyond the start of the leave.

# HR guidance: parental leave changes for 2027

This guidance is restricted to HR and people managers until the change is announced on February 15, 2027. From March 1, 2027, paid parental leave increases from 16 to 20 weeks and can be taken in up to three blocks.

The six-month service requirement and full pay are unchanged. Employees whose leave starts before March 1, 2027 stay on the 2024 policy. Managers should send questions to their HR business partner.

## Questions managers may hear

Employees may ask whether they can split leave they have already started. They can't: the three-block rule applies only to leave that starts on or after March 1, 2027.

Employees on fixed-term contracts receive the same leave if their contract runs for at least six months beyond the start of the leave.

Employees with at least six months of service receive 16 weeks of paid parental leave after the birth or adoption of a child. The leave must be taken in one continuous block within 12 months of the birth or adoption, at 100 percent of base salary.

evidence.title: Safety bulletin SB-0932: Seal housing work
evidence.section: Safety bulletin SB-0932: Seal housing work

segments.text:
# Safety bulletin SB-0932: Seal housing work

Issued after a near miss at the Riverside plant in 2026, when a seal housing was opened on a pump that was still under seal-water pressure.

Apply lockout/tagout (LOTO) to the motor and isolate the seal-water and process lines before opening any CP-200 seal housing. Verify zero energy before work starts.

Zero energy means that the motor can't start from the panel, the local pressure gauges read zero and the casing drain is open. Each person working on the pump fits their own lock.

This bulletin applies to every pump with a mechanical seal flushed by seal water, not only to the CP-200. Supervisors brief their teams on it before the next seal job and record the briefing.

At the Riverside plant, report any seal-water line that can't be isolated or drained to the Riverside maintenance planner on extension 4410 before work starts.

evidence.title: CP-200 Centrifugal Pump Operating and Maintenance Manual
evidence.section: CP-200 Centrifugal Pump Operating and Maintenance Manual › 5 Commissioning › 5.1 Checks before the first start

segments.text:
# 5 Commissioning

## 5.1 Checks before the first start

1. Check that the rotating assembly turns freely by hand.
2. Check the coupling alignment and fit the coupling guard.
3. Check that the bearings are greased; pumps leave the factory greased for 4,000 hours.
4. Flush the suction pipe and the seal-water line before connecting them.

## 5.4 Start-up

Before the first start, and after any work on the seal or the impeller, prime the pump and check the seal-water supply.

1. Open the suction valve fully. Never throttle the suction side.
2. Vent the casing at the vent plug until water flows without air.
3. Open the seal-water supply and confirm a pressure of 2.0 to 3.0 bar at the seal flush connection. The seal-water pressure must exceed the suction pressure by at least 1 bar.
4. Open the discharge valve about one quarter.
5. Jog the motor and confirm the direction of rotation against the arrow on the bearing housing.
6. Start the pump, then open the discharge valve slowly to the duty point within two minutes. Running against a closed discharge valve for longer overheats the liquid in the casing.

During the first hour, check that the bearing temperatures stay below 80 °C and listen for cavitation noise.

## 4.2 Pipework

Support the suction and discharge pipes independently of the pump; the pump flanges must carry no pipe loads. Fit a strainer in the suction line during the first weeks of operation and remove it once the system is clean.

evidence.section: CP-200 Troubleshooting Guide › 3 Mechanical problems › Cavitation

segments.text:
## Cavitation

Cavitation is the collapse of vapor bubbles that form where the pressure at the impeller inlet falls below the liquid's vapor pressure. It sounds like gravel rattling in the casing and erodes the impeller vanes within weeks.

Check the suction side first: the suction valve must be fully open, the suction strainer clean and the tank level above its minimum. If the pump runs far to the right of its curve, throttle the discharge valve back to the duty point.

# Engineering change notice ECN-2291

| Field | Entry |

| Change notice | ECN-2291 |
| Title | CP-200 mechanical seal |
| Product | CP-200 centrifugal pump, all sizes |
| Originator | Nadia Rahman, reliability engineering |
| Date raised | August 21, 2026 |
| Effective | September 14, 2026 |

Effective September 14, 2026, mechanical seal PN-4471-B is superseded by PN-4471-C on all CP-200 pumps. PN-4471-C has a silicon-carbide face rated for higher seal-water temperatures. Fit PN-4471-C at the next seal replacement and quarantine remaining PN-4471-B stock.

Affected documents: CP-200 manual (2009) sections 7.2 and 8.1, and SOP-FS-014. The manual will be revised in 2027; until then, this notice takes precedence over it.

Approved by Nadia Rahman, reliability engineering.

|---|---|---|
| PN-4471-B | PN-4471-C | Quarantine remaining stock; return to Fabrikam Seals for credit |

evidence.section: SOP-FS-014: Mechanical seal replacement on CP-200 pumps

segments.text:
# SOP-FS-014: Mechanical seal replacement on CP-200 pumps

Revision 3, effective September 14, 2026. This revision replaces PN-4471-B with PN-4471-C, following ECN-2291.

1. Apply lockout/tagout to the motor and isolate the seal-water and process lines, as safety bulletin SB-0932 requires. Verify zero energy.
2. Drain the casing and remove the coupling guard.
3. Remove the seal housing and the old seal. Inspect the shaft sleeve for scoring.
4. Fit mechanical seal PN-4471-C. Don't mix PN-4471-B and PN-4471-C parts.
5. Tighten the seal gland nuts evenly to 25 N·m.
6. Refit the coupling guard, remove the locks and tags, and start the pump as described in section 5.4 of the manual.
7. Record the seal's part number and the operating hours in the work order.

segments.text:
## Why seals fail

- Dry running, even for a few seconds
- Seal-water pressure below 1.5 bar (error E-217 trips the pump)
- Abrasive particles in the seal water
- Carbon face wear above 60 °C seal-water temperature

evidence.title: WI-FS-031: Cleaning the seal-water strainer upstream of V-114
evidence.section: WI-FS-031: Cleaning the seal-water strainer upstream of V-114

segments.text:
# WI-FS-031: Cleaning the seal-water strainer upstream of V-114

The seal-water line to pump P-201 has a Y-strainer with a 100-micron screen upstream of valve V-114. A blocked screen is the most common cause of error E-217 at the Riverside plant.

1. Stop P-201 and close the isolation valve upstream of the strainer. Leave V-114 open.
2. Put a bucket under the strainer and release the pressure through the blow-down valve.
3. Unscrew the strainer cap, pull out the screen and rinse it with clean water. Replace the screen if it is torn.
4. Refit the screen with a new cap gasket and open the isolation valve.
5. Check that the gauge shows a seal-water pressure of 2.0 to 3.0 bar.

Clean the screen every three months, and whenever E-217 trips.

# Safety bulletin SB-0947: Hot work permits

Welding, grinding and cutting outside the workshops need a hot work permit from the shift supervisor. Remove or cover combustible material within 10 meters, keep a fire extinguisher at the work site and post a fire watch for 60 minutes after the work ends.

Hot work on a line that has carried oil or solvent also needs a gas test before the permit is signed.

The permit is valid for one shift. If the work isn't finished by the end of the shift, the next shift supervisor issues a new permit after checking the site again.

# Safety bulletin SB-0950: Chemical cleaning of strainers

Some sites descale seal-water strainer screens with citric acid solution. Wear chemical goggles and nitrile gloves, and mix the solution in the workshop, never at the pump.

Rinse the screen with clean water before refitting it; acid left on the screen attacks the mechanical seal's elastomers. WI-FS-031 describes the strainer cleaning itself.

# Safety bulletin SB-0901: Confined space entry

Pump pits, tanks and valve chambers are confined spaces. Enter one only with a confined space permit, a gas test that shows at least 19.5 percent oxygen and no flammable or toxic gas, and an attendant who stays outside.

The attendant keeps a log of everyone inside and calls the emergency team if anyone inside stops responding. The attendant never goes in to rescue.

segments.text:
## Error E-301: suction pressure sensor fault

Error E-301 means the signal from suction pressure transmitter PT-11 is outside 4 to 20 mA. The pump keeps running without low-suction protection, so the controller raises an alarm.

Causes, most likely first:

1. A broken transmitter cable.
2. A failed transmitter.

Check the cable and replace PT-11 if its output stays out of range.

evidence.section: SOP-FS-014: Mechanical seal replacement on CP-200 pumps

segments.text:
# SOP-FS-014: Mechanical seal replacement on CP-200 pumps

Revision 3, effective September 14, 2026. This revision replaces PN-4471-B with PN-4471-C, following ECN-2291.

1. Apply lockout/tagout to the motor and isolate the seal-water and process lines, as safety bulletin SB-0932 requires. Verify zero energy.
2. Drain the casing and remove the coupling guard.
3. Remove the seal housing and the old seal. Inspect the shaft sleeve for scoring.
4. Fit mechanical seal PN-4471-C. Don't mix PN-4471-B and PN-4471-C parts.
5. Tighten the seal gland nuts evenly to 25 N·m.
6. Refit the coupling guard, remove the locks and tags, and start the pump as described in section 5.4 of the manual.
7. Record the seal's part number and the operating hours in the work order.

## 7.2 Service intervals

Inspect the mechanical seal and the bearings every 2,000 operating hours or six months, whichever comes first. Replace mechanical seal PN-4471-B every 8,000 operating hours.

| Task | Interval |
|---|---|
| Inspect the mechanical seal and the bearings | 2,000 h or 6 months |
| Regrease the bearings (lithium-complex grease, 15 g per bearing) | 4,000 h |
| Check the coupling alignment | 12 months |
| Replace mechanical seal PN-4471-B | 8,000 h |
| Replace the bearings | 32,000 h |

Record every inspection in the maintenance log with the operating hours from the hour meter. Halve the intervals for pumps that handle abrasive liquids or run above 60 °C.

segments.text:
## Why seals fail

- Dry running, even for a few seconds
- Seal-water pressure below 1.5 bar (error E-217 trips the pump)
- Abrasive particles in the seal water
- Carbon face wear above 60 °C seal-water temperature

In 2026, three PN-4471-B failures at Riverside were traced to carbon face wear at seal-water temperatures above 60 °C. That is why ECN-2291 introduced PN-4471-C with a silicon-carbide face.

segments.text:
## 6.3 Flange bolt torque

Table 6-2 gives the tightening torque for the CP-200 flange bolts. The values apply to bolts of property class 8.8, lightly oiled, with the spiral-wound gaskets supplied with the pump.

| Bolt size | Torque |
|---|---|
| M10 | 49 N·m |
| M12 | 85 N·m |
| M16 | 210 N·m |

Tighten the M12 flange bolts (property class 8.8, lightly oiled) to 85 N·m. Apply the torque in a cross pattern in three passes: 30 N·m, 60 N·m, then 85 N·m. Re-check the torque after the first 24 hours of operation.

Don't reuse spiral-wound gaskets. A gasket that has been compressed once won't seal at the specified torque.

## 6.4 Seal housing bolts

Tighten the four seal housing bolts to 45 N·m. Fit the seal housing before the bearing housing is bolted back to the casing, so that the seal can be centered on the shaft.

evidence.title: CP-200 Troubleshooting Guide
evidence.section: CP-200 Troubleshooting Guide › 2 Controller error codes › Error E-201: suction pressure low

segments.text:
## Error E-201: suction pressure low

Error E-201 means the suction pressure fell below 0.3 bar. The controller warns for 20 seconds before it trips the pump, to ride through short dips.

Causes, most likely first:

1. The suction valve is partly closed.
2. The suction strainer is blocked.
3. The level in the suction tank is too low.

Open the suction valve fully, clean the suction strainer and check the tank level before resetting E-201.

evidence.section: SOP-FS-014: Mechanical seal replacement on CP-200 pumps

segments.text:
# SOP-FS-014: Mechanical seal replacement on CP-200 pumps

Revision 3, effective September 14, 2026. This revision replaces PN-4471-B with PN-4471-C, following ECN-2291.

1. Apply lockout/tagout to the motor and isolate the seal-water and process lines, as safety bulletin SB-0932 requires. Verify zero energy.
2. Drain the casing and remove the coupling guard.
3. Remove the seal housing and the old seal. Inspect the shaft sleeve for scoring.
4. Fit mechanical seal PN-4471-C. Don't mix PN-4471-B and PN-4471-C parts.
5. Tighten the seal gland nuts evenly to 25 N·m.
6. Refit the coupling guard, remove the locks and tags, and start the pump as described in section 5.4 of the manual.
7. Record the seal's part number and the operating hours in the work order.

evidence.title: WI-FS-031: Cleaning the seal-water strainer upstream of V-114
evidence.section: WI-FS-031: Cleaning the seal-water strainer upstream of V-114

segments.text:
# WI-FS-031: Cleaning the seal-water strainer upstream of V-114

The seal-water line to pump P-201 has a Y-strainer with a 100-micron screen upstream of valve V-114. A blocked screen is the most common cause of error E-217 at the Riverside plant.

1. Stop P-201 and close the isolation valve upstream of the strainer. Leave V-114 open.
2. Put a bucket under the strainer and release the pressure through the blow-down valve.
3. Unscrew the strainer cap, pull out the screen and rinse it with clean water. Replace the screen if it is torn.
4. Refit the screen with a new cap gasket and open the isolation valve.
5. Check that the gauge shows a seal-water pressure of 2.0 to 3.0 bar.

Clean the screen every three months, and whenever E-217 trips.

# Engineering change notice ECN-2240

| Field | Entry |

| Change notice | ECN-2240 |
| Title | CP-200 casing wear ring material |
| Product | CP-200 centrifugal pump, all sizes |
| Originator | Nadia Rahman, reliability engineering |
| Date raised | January 27, 2025 |
| Effective | March 1, 2025 |

Effective March 1, 2025, casing wear ring PN-2840-A (bronze) is superseded by PN-2840-B (carbon-filled PTFE composite) on all CP-200 pumps. The composite ring tolerates brief dry running without seizing, and its smaller running clearance of 0.25 mm improves efficiency by about 2 percent.

Fit PN-2840-B whenever a wear ring is replaced. The bronze rings in stock may be used up on pumps that handle liquids above 80 °C, where the composite ring is not approved.

Affected parts

| Old part | New part | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| PN-2840-A | PN-2840-B | Use up stock on pumps above 80 °C only |

## Error E-103: wrong phase sequence

Error E-103 means the supply phase sequence is reversed, so the pump would run backwards. The controller blocks the start; it never trips a running pump for E-103.

Causes, most likely first:

## Error E-101: motor overload

Error E-101 means the motor current stayed above the overload setting for longer than the trip delay. The overload relay trips after 10 seconds above 110 percent of the motor's rated current.

Causes, most likely first:

1. The pump runs far to the right of its curve because the discharge valve is open too far.
2. The impeller rubs on the wear ring after a bearing failure.
3. The overload relay is set below the motor's rated current.

Find and remove the cause, then reset E-101 at the local panel. The relay resets itself after two minutes.

evidence.section: CP-200 Centrifugal Pump Operating and Maintenance Manual › 2 Description

segments.text:
# 2 Description

The CP-200 is a single-stage, end-suction centrifugal pump with a closed impeller, designed for clean or slightly contaminated water at up to 90 °C. The pump and its motor sit on a common baseplate and are joined by a flexible spacer coupling, so the rotating assembly can be removed without disturbing the pipework.

The shaft is sealed by a cartridge mechanical seal flushed with clean seal water from an external supply. Two grease-lubricated ball bearings in the bearing housing carry the shaft. A controller on the pump skid monitors the motor, the bearing temperatures and the seal-water pressure and trips the pump when a limit is exceeded.

|---|---|

| Speed | 1,480 rpm at 50 Hz |
| Motor power | 15 to 45 kW |
| Seal-water pressure | 2.0 to 3.0 bar |
| Weight of the pump without motor | 310 kg |

Before the first start, and after any work on the seal or the impeller, prime the pump and check the seal-water supply.

segments.text:
## Error E-201: suction pressure low

Error E-201 means the suction pressure fell below 0.3 bar. The controller warns for 20 seconds before it trips the pump, to ride through short dips.

Causes, most likely first:

1. The suction valve is partly closed.
2. The suction strainer is blocked.
3. The level in the suction tank is too low.

Open the suction valve fully, clean the suction strainer and check the tank level before resetting E-201.

evidence.title: CP-200 Troubleshooting Guide
evidence.section: CP-200 Troubleshooting Guide › 2 Controller error codes › Error E-217: seal-water pressure low

segments.text:
## Error E-217: seal-water pressure low

Error E-217 means seal-water pressure low. The controller trips the pump when seal-water pressure stays below 1.5 bar for 10 seconds, to protect the mechanical seal. Check that seal-water valve V-114 is open and that its strainer is clean, then reset the alarm at the local panel.

Common causes, most likely first:

1. Seal-water valve V-114 left closed or partly closed after maintenance.
2. A blocked strainer upstream of V-114 (work instruction WI-FS-031 describes the cleaning).
3. A failed pressure switch PS-31. Compare its reading with the local gauge.

To clear E-217, restore the seal-water pressure to at least 2.0 bar, wait until the alarm light stops flashing, then press RESET on the local panel. If the alarm returns within an hour, don't restart the pump again; raise a work order for the seal-water system.

evidence.title: SOP-FS-014: Mechanical seal replacement on CP-200 pumps
evidence.section: SOP-FS-014: Mechanical seal replacement on CP-200 pumps

segments.text:
# SOP-FS-014: Mechanical seal replacement on CP-200 pumps

Revision 3, effective September 14, 2026. This revision replaces PN-4471-B with PN-4471-C, following ECN-2291.

1. Apply lockout/tagout to the motor and isolate the seal-water and process lines, as safety bulletin SB-0932 requires. Verify zero energy.
2. Drain the casing and remove the coupling guard.
3. Remove the seal housing and the old seal. Inspect the shaft sleeve for scoring.
4. Fit mechanical seal PN-4471-C. Don't mix PN-4471-B and PN-4471-C parts.
5. Tighten the seal gland nuts evenly to 25 N·m.
6. Refit the coupling guard, remove the locks and tags, and start the pump as described in section 5.4 of the manual.
7. Record the seal's part number and the operating hours in the work order.

segments.text:
# 9 Troubleshooting

The controller shows an error code for most faults; the CP-200 troubleshooting guide explains each code. Table 9-1 lists faults that the controller can't detect.

Table 9-1 Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Possible cause | Remedy |
|---|---|---|
| Pump doesn't deliver | Suction valve closed or casing not vented | Open the suction valve fully and vent the casing |
| Delivery falls off over weeks | Worn wear ring or impeller | Check the impeller clearance (section 6.2) |
| High bearing temperature | Too much or too little grease | Regrease as section 7.3 describes |
| Seal leaks steadily | Worn seal faces | Replace the mechanical seal (section 8.1) |
| Motor overloads | Pump runs far right of its curve | Throttle the discharge valve to the duty point |

evidence.title: CP-200 Centrifugal Pump Operating and Maintenance Manual
evidence.section: CP-200 Centrifugal Pump Operating and Maintenance Manual › 2 Description

segments.text:
# 2 Description

The CP-200 is a single-stage, end-suction centrifugal pump with a closed impeller, designed for clean or slightly contaminated water at up to 90 °C. The pump and its motor sit on a common baseplate and are joined by a flexible spacer coupling, so the rotating assembly can be removed without disturbing the pipework.

The shaft is sealed by a cartridge mechanical seal flushed with clean seal water from an external supply. Two grease-lubricated ball bearings in the bearing housing carry the shaft. A controller on the pump skid monitors the motor, the bearing temperatures and the seal-water pressure and trips the pump when a limit is exceeded.

evidence.section: CP-200 Troubleshooting Guide › 2 Controller error codes › Error E-310: communication lost

segments.text:
## Error E-310: communication lost

Error E-310 means the controller hasn't heard from the plant control system for 30 seconds. The pump keeps running at its last set point.

Causes, most likely first:

1. A network fault.
2. The plant control system was restarted.

E-310 clears itself when communication returns.

evidence.title: CP-200 Troubleshooting Guide
evidence.section: CP-200 Troubleshooting Guide › 2 Controller error codes › Error E-105: earth fault

segments.text:
## Error E-105: earth fault

Error E-105 means the controller measured a leakage current to earth above 300 mA. The earth-fault relay trips the pump at once.

Causes, most likely first:

1. Water in the motor terminal box.
2. Damaged motor cable insulation.

Don't reset E-105 until an electrician has measured the motor's insulation resistance.

evidence.title: CP-200 Troubleshooting Guide
evidence.section: CP-200 Troubleshooting Guide › 2 Controller error codes › Error E-204: flow low

segments.text:
## Error E-204: flow low

Error E-204 means the flow fell below 40 m³/h, the pump's minimum continuous flow. The controller warns at once and trips the pump after 2 minutes of low flow.

Causes, most likely first:

1. The discharge valve is throttled too far.
2. The process no longer needs the pump.

Open the discharge valve or stop the pump, then reset E-204.

segments.text:
## Error E-221: bearing temperature high

Error E-221 means a bearing temperature exceeded 95 °C. The controller warns at 85 °C and trips the pump at 95 °C.

Causes, most likely first:

1. Too much grease after regreasing.
2. Misalignment between pump and motor.
3. A worn bearing.

Let the bearings cool, check the alignment and the amount of grease, then reset E-221.

## Error E-303: bearing temperature sensor fault

Error E-303 means one of the bearing temperature sensors TE-21 and TE-22 reports an open circuit. The pump keeps running without bearing temperature protection on that bearing.

Causes, most likely first:

1. A loose sensor connector.
2. A failed sensor.

Reseat the connector; replace the sensor if E-303 returns.

evidence.title: CP-200 Troubleshooting Guide
evidence.section: CP-200 Troubleshooting Guide › 3 Mechanical problems › Troubleshooting: excessive vibration

segments.text:
# 3 Mechanical problems

## Troubleshooting: excessive vibration

Vibration above 4.5 mm/s RMS on the bearing housing needs investigation; above 7.1 mm/s RMS, stop the pump.

Likely causes, in the order to check them:

- Misalignment between the pump and motor shafts after maintenance. Check the coupling alignment.
- Cavitation, which sounds like gravel rattling in the casing. It comes from low suction pressure: check that the suction valve is fully open and the suction strainer is clean.
- Worn bearings. Bearing noise rises before the vibration does.
- A loose baseplate or loose foot bolts.
- A damaged or unbalanced impeller.

evidence.section: CP-200 Troubleshooting Guide › 2 Controller error codes › Error E-231: liquid temperature high

segments.text:
## Error E-231: liquid temperature high

Error E-231 means the liquid temperature in the casing exceeded 90 °C. The controller trips the pump after 10 seconds above the limit.

Causes, most likely first:

1. The pump ran against a closed discharge valve.
2. The process supplies liquid hotter than the pump's rating.

Let the casing cool and find out why the liquid overheated before resetting E-231.

evidence.title: HG-400 Helical Gearbox Operating Manual
evidence.section: HG-400 Helical Gearbox Operating Manual › 2 Product description

segments.text:
# 2 Product description

The HG-400 is a foot-mounted helical gearbox with parallel input and output shafts. Hardened and ground helical gears run in an oil bath, and tapered roller bearings carry the shafts. The housing is cast iron with cooling fins on both sides.

## 2.1 Type designation

The type code on the nameplate gives the frame size, the number of stages and the nominal ratio. For example, HG-400-2-12.5 is a two-stage gearbox with a ratio of 12.5 to 1.

Table 2-1 Ratings at 1,500 rpm input

| Ratio | Stages | Output torque | Thermal rating |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5.6 | 2 | 4,200 N·m | 55 kW |
| 8 | 2 | 4,400 N·m | 48 kW |
| 12.5 | 2 | 4,600 N·m | 40 kW |
| 16 | 2 | 4,600 N·m | 35 kW |
| 25 | 3 | 4,800 N·m | 28 kW |
| 40 | 3 | 5,000 N·m | 22 kW |

The thermal rating is the power the gearbox can transmit continuously without the oil exceeding 90 °C at an ambient temperature of 25 °C. Above 35 °C ambient, derate it by 10 percent for every 5 °C.

evidence.title: HG-400 Helical Gearbox Operating Manual
evidence.section: HG-400 Helical Gearbox Operating Manual › 3 Installation › 3.2 Mounting

segments.text:
## 3.2 Mounting

Mount the HG-400 on a flat, rigid base; the mounting surface must be flat to within 0.1 mm. Use the four M16 foot bolts of property class 8.8 and tighten them to 195 N·m in a cross pattern.

Put shims under the feet, never under the gearbox housing. After mounting, align the input and output couplings as their installation instructions describe, and check that the breather plug on top of the housing is fitted and open.

## 3.3 Shaft connections

Fit couplings and sprockets by heating them to about 100 °C; never hammer them onto the shafts, because the impact damages the bearings. Keep the overhung load on the output shaft within the value on the nameplate.

## 3.2 Mounting

Mount the HG-400 on a flat, rigid base; the mounting surface must be flat to within 0.1 mm. Use the four M16 foot bolts of property class 8.8 and tighten them to 195 N·m in a cross pattern.

Put shims under the feet, never under the gearbox housing. After mounting, align the input and output couplings as their installation instructions describe, and check that the breather plug on top of the housing is fitted and open.

## 3.3 Shaft connections

Fit couplings and sprockets by heating them to about 100 °C; never hammer them onto the shafts, because the impact damages the bearings. Keep the overhung load on the output shaft within the value on the nameplate.

# 4 Lubrication

## 4.1 Lubrication

The HG-400 is filled at the factory with 18 liters of ISO VG 220 mineral gear oil. Change the oil after the first 500 operating hours, then every 5,000 operating hours or every 12 months, whichever comes first. Synthetic PAO oil of the same viscosity extends the interval to 10,000 hours.

Check the oil level weekly at the sight glass with the gearbox stopped. In operation, the oil temperature must not exceed 90 °C.

## 4.2 Approved oils

Table 4-1 Approved oils

| Oil type | Viscosity grade | Change interval |
|---|---|---|
| Mineral gear oil | ISO VG 220 | 5,000 h or 12 months |
| Synthetic PAO gear oil | ISO VG 220 | 10,000 h or 24 months |
| Food-grade gear oil (NSF H1) | ISO VG 220 | 5,000 h or 12 months |

Don't mix mineral and synthetic oils. When changing from one type to the other, flush the gearbox with the new oil first.

segments.text:
# SOP-MS-003: Oil change on HG-400 gearboxes

Revision 2, effective January 20, 2025. This procedure applies the oil change in section 4.3 of the HG-400 manual at Contoso plants and adds the checks that the plants' oil analysis program needs.

1. Lock out the driving motor as SOP-FS-007 describes for pumps; the same steps apply to gearboxes.
2. Take an oil sample from the middle of the sight glass level before draining, and label it with the gearbox tag.
3. Drain the warm oil, then clean and inspect the magnetic drain plug.
4. Refill with ISO VG 220 oil of the type on the gearbox's lubrication label: 18 liters for an HG-400.
5. Run the gearbox for ten minutes and check the level and the plugs for leaks.
6. Record the oil type, the quantity and the operating hours in the work order, and send the sample to the laboratory.

Gearbox GBX-07 on the Lakeside packaging line runs on synthetic PAO oil, so its change interval is 10,000 hours.

| Symptom | Possible cause | Remedy |

| Oil temperature above 90 °C | Overload, wrong oil or dirty cooling fins | Check the load and the oil; clean the fins |
| Foam in the sight glass | Water in the oil or mixed oils | Change the oil and find the source of water |

# Field service report SR-2026-1130

Customer: Woodgrove Foods, cold store 1. Engineer: Kwame Asante. Date: November 30, 2026.

Complaint: the evaporator fan drive stopped several times a night with fault F002.

Findings: the ramp-down time had been set to 1 second after a controller upgrade, too short for the fan's inertia.

Work done: raised parameter 2-11 (ramp-down time) to 20 seconds. No further F002 faults in 48 hours of logging.
